A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study, with matching authors, method, and original results. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable, allowing additions to be distinguished from relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-compression experiments, capacity measurements, scaling experiments, and embedding-geometry analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Mamba results and experiments with conventional compression algorithms.

M1.justification: Both versions optimize per-text memory vectors through next-token cross-entropy while freezing the language model, then decode from those vectors. Appendix C in v2 explicitly applies the same procedure to Mamba; no new algorithmic component is introduced.

E1.justification: PG-19, post-October-2024 fanfiction, randomly sampled GloVe words, and the GovReport embedding analysis already appear in v1. v2 reuses this coverage; its additions concern model configurations and compression metrics rather than new data populations or task requirements.

E2.justification: Appendix F and Table 4 introduce an evaluated comparison with zlib, bz2, lzma, Huffman coding, and arithmetic coding using Pythia-160M. Their storage-compression ratios contextualize the proposed representation's bit cost. v1 contains no corresponding codec comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds four Mamba configurations, from 130M to 1.4B parameters, and a storage-compression evaluation using original size divided by compressed size in bits. These substantially extend the evaluation settings. The original reconstruction thresholds, sampling account, length grids, and optimization budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Section 4.6 and Appendix C test whether the entropy-capacity patterns extend beyond Transformers, while Appendix F examines whether reducing input-vector count produces storage savings. Existing text-complexity, vector-count scaling, cosine-similarity, and interpolation analyses are retained; the geometry analysis moves from Appendix D to E.

E5.justification: Existing plus/minus reporting, Figure 4's standard-deviation bands, and the multiple-initialization geometry analysis remain unchanged. Added result rows continue uncertainty reporting without introducing new seed information, repeated-run counts, significance tests, or estimation procedures.

E6.justification: Table 3 adds Mamba outcomes, including Mamba-1.4B capacities of 512 PG-19 tokens and 288 random-text tokens. Table 4 adds codec results, including 6.77 ± 0.75 for arithmetic coding with Pythia-160M on PG-19; Appendix F reports approximately 0.8x storage compression for the embedding representation. Original Table 1 and the headline 1568- and 7168-token results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The capacity bound, metric definitions in Equations 1–4, and capacity-utilization definition are unchanged. Appendix F introduces an empirical storage-size comparison, without adding or revising formal bounds, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The four stated contributions and central abstract/conclusion claims remain: approximately 1500 tokens per vector, capacity tied to cross-entropy, and approximately linear scaling with vector count. The abstract clarifies the computational objective without changing these contribution claims.

C2.justification: Appendix F materially qualifies the compression interpretation: 1568x fewer embeddings corresponds to approximately 0.8x storage compression, so the vector occupies more bits than raw text. v2 also interprets Mamba results as evidence of applicability beyond Transformers and discusses its increasing capacity utilization with model size.

D1.justification: Table 2 adds Mamba checkpoint identifiers, parameter counts, embedding dimensions, and vocabulary sizes. Appendix F specifies bfloat16 for the Llama-3.1-8B storage calculation. Optimizer settings, training budget, hardware, data collection instructions, and the code link remain unchanged.

R1.justification: Related work gains focused coverage of KV-cache compression, including H2O, SnapKV, Nugget, Dodo, and KV-Distill, plus an explicit distinction from Delétang et al.'s bitstream compression. Mamba and state-space references are added. The existing positioning remains largely intact; publication updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording and terminology edits, including changing 'Single Token' to 'Single Vector,' and adds acknowledgments. Section 4.6 and Appendices C and F extend the existing structure, while former Appendices C and D become D and E. Most original prose and organization are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds the comprehensive results Table 3 and codec Table 4, expands Table 2, and extends Figures 5 and 6 with Mamba results. Figure 6 is reorganized onto a separate page. Original Table 1, Figures 3–4, and the geometry plots remain visually unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through Mamba experiments and makes the compression claim easier to interpret: Appendix F explicitly distinguishes fewer input vectors from disk-space savings and reports the approximately 0.8x storage ratio. The codec comparisons and consolidated results table improve assessability. These are useful supporting improvements to a study whose central method and headline findings remain unchanged.
